name: Cell Thawing
description: Rapid thawing and recovery of cryopreserved mammalian cells from liquid nitrogen storage. Speed is critical — DMSO is toxic at warm temperatures. Work efficiently.
source_note: General educational template for thawing cryopreserved mammalian cells.

steps.title: Prepare and warm culture medium
steps.description: Pre-warm complete cell culture medium to 37°C in a water bath. Prepare a new labeled culture flask. Have centrifuge ready at room temperature.
steps.notes: Prepare everything before retrieving vial from liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Retrieve vial from liquid nitrogen
steps.description: Retrieve cryovial from liquid nitrogen storage. Note: if using liquid-phase LN₂ storage, allow vial to equilibrate briefly in vapor phase before opening to prevent pressurized explosion.
steps.notes: Move quickly from LN₂ to the 37°C water bath. Every second counts.
steps.warnings: CRITICAL SAFETY: If vial was stored in liquid phase LN₂, liquid nitrogen may have entered vial. Hold vial at arm's length and loosen cap slowly in a fume hood to release pressure before warming. Explosion risk if not vented.

steps.title: Thaw rapidly in 37°C water bath
steps.description: Immerse cryovial in 37°C water bath. Swirl gently until the ice crystal just melts (1–2 min). Do not allow to fully warm up — remove when a small ice crystal remains.
steps.notes: Remove from water bath when a tiny ice crystal is still visible. Over-warming increases DMSO toxicity.
steps.warnings: Rapid thawing is essential for cell viability. Do not leave unattended.

steps.title: Dilute cells into warm medium (dropwise)
steps.description: Transfer thawed cell suspension to a 15 mL tube containing 9 mL of pre-warmed complete medium. Add dropwise while gently swirling to dilute DMSO slowly (prevents osmotic shock).
steps.notes: Dropwise dilution minimizes osmotic shock from DMSO removal. Final DMSO concentration should be <1%.

steps.title: Centrifuge to remove DMSO
steps.description: Centrifuge to pellet cells. Remove supernatant containing DMSO completely. This step removes residual DMSO which is toxic to cells in culture.

steps.title: Resuspend in complete medium
steps.description: Aspirate supernatant. Gently resuspend cell pellet in 5–10 mL of fresh complete medium. Pipette gently to avoid cell damage.

steps.title: Transfer to culture flask
steps.description: Transfer cell suspension to a pre-labeled culture flask. Rock gently to distribute cells evenly. Place in 37°C, 5% CO₂ incubator.
steps.notes: Label flask: cell line, passage number, date, source vial ID.

steps.title: Check attachment and change media next day
steps.description: Check cells under microscope after 4–6 hours and the next morning for attachment and morphology. Change medium after 24 h to remove dead cells and remaining DMSO traces.
steps.notes: Some cell lines take 24–48 h to fully recover and resume normal growth. Low initial attachment or slow growth is normal after thawing — do not re-passage too early.
